note: Wild first harvest. Rank later. Prices are street estimates in EUR, not quotes.

items.sees: Broadcast Remote ID on Bluetooth and Wi-Fi, where the phone radio can hear it
items.misses: Fibre-optic FPV, military links, many sub-250 g C0 drones, anything that stays dark
items.risk: none as a listener. The phone SoC is usually Asian. That does not matter for a weekend test.

items.sees: ASTM F3411 / EN 4709-002 Remote ID over Wi-Fi and BLE. Firmware such as RID_Scanner tracks dozens of UAVs at once.
items.misses: Anything that does not broadcast RID. Also a Chinese MCU on a German roof.
items.risk: The SoC is the problem, not the USB cable. Fine for a first listener. Not a trusted node until a European MCU path exists.

items.sees: The public RID message types on Bluetooth 4/5, Wi-Fi Beacon and Wi-Fi NaN
items.misses: Proprietary DJI DroneID on OcuSync
items.risk: None. This is the protocol, not a chip.

items.sees: Makes a test drone visible. Bluetooth 4 and 5, claimed range up to 3 km, 1.5 g.
items.misses: It is a transmitter for your own aircraft, not a scanner.
items.risk: EU company, EASA DRI path. Use it so the home test actually broadcasts.

items.sees: EU Declaration of Conformity on the EASA DRI module list
items.misses: Scanner duty. This is for the aircraft under test.
items.risk: Poland, EU. Better origin than a nameless board from a marketplace.

items.sees: Propeller harmonic comb, including fibre-optic FPV that emits no radio
items.misses: Direction, if the array is only 79 mm across. VolAnti uses four mics as a sensitivity device, not a bearing finder.
items.risk: MEMS capsules are a commodity. The firmware and the box matter more than the flag on the reel.

items.sees: Multirotor rotor noise. Breadboard build about 40 GBP in an evening.
items.misses: Long-range bearing. No intercept. No RID decode.
items.risk: The published box uses an ESP32-S3. Same MCU tension as the RID receiver.

items.design: Cambridge, UK. In-house silicon on the Pi 5.
items.make: Sony UK Technology Centre, Pencoed, Wales
items.sees: Whatever you plug in: RID dongle, mics, camera, SDR. This is the node brain.
items.misses: The board is assembled in Wales. Many passives and the wider silicon still travel.
items.risk: Best default brain in Europe that a citizen can buy on Monday. Not a German chip. Not a Chinese board either.

items.sees: Confirmation of a track you already have. Birds, airliners, clouds.
items.misses: First detection. Looking up at a 20 cm quad at 400 m is a hard vision problem.
items.risk: Sony IMX sensor. Confirmation layer, never the only layer.

items.sees: ADS-B at 1090 MHz, some analog video, lower bands. Cheap spectrum ears.
items.misses: 2.4 GHz and 5.8 GHz drone links. The R820T2 tops out near 1.8 GHz. An RTL-SDR will not hear OcuSync.
items.risk: Useful and misunderstood. Do not buy it expecting DJI downlink. Tuner silicon is Taiwan/China.

items.sees: 1 MHz to 6 GHz. Enough to sit on 2.4 and 5.8 GHz. Used in DJI DroneID research (RUB DroneSecurity, NDSS 2023) with wider SDRs.
items.misses: Coherent direction finding (one radio, one ear). Half-duplex.
items.risk: US open hardware. Right class of radio for a serious RF node. Still not a German radio.

items.sees: Direction of arrival on the bands the tuners cover
items.misses: Same frequency ceiling as RTL-SDR. Not a 2.4 GHz OcuSync DF.
items.risk: The coherent array idea is right. The tuner band is wrong for consumer drone video.

items.sees: Company figures: consumer UAV detection out to 40 km, military UAV 80 km, 400 MHz to 6 GHz (options wider). Hawk T1 airborne Blind-TDoA shown at Eurosatory 2026. 700+ installed systems claimed, including Heathrow.
items.misses: Not a citizen weekend kit. This is the German professional RF layer.
items.risk: German EW house. This is the kind of radio a cell graduates to, not the kind you 3D-print.

items.sees: 60 GHz FMCW, 1 Tx + 3 Rx in package. Datasheet max detection 15 m. Presence, gesture, people counting.
items.misses: The sky. 15 m is a room, a balcony, a hovering quad over the garden table. It is not an inbound Shahed.
items.risk: German chip, right company, wrong range for a city shield. Keep it for close-in confirmation, not as 'the radar'.

items.sees: X-band AESA, micro-Doppler classing of small UAVs vs birds vs helicopters. 120° per panel, 360° with three. Track-while-scan >300 targets / 120°. In Bundeswehr C-UAS (Boxer / Kongsberg), ASUL, HoWiSM, NNbS. Antenna about 36 kg.
items.misses: A rooftop of a family house. This is layer two: Feuerwehr, THW, Bundeswehr.
items.risk: German military radar. The plug-in we want later, not the first node.

items.make: DE, plus lines in Ukraine and the US
items.sees: ISR, not intercept. VTOL fixed wing, hours of endurance, combat hours in Ukraine. Blue UAS list 2025. Company C-UAS interceptor work with Airbus H145M is a 2026 thread, not a shop SKU.
items.misses: Net catching over a German suburb. Wrong job for week one.
items.risk: The German airframe house to talk to. Recon and later mother-drone / high sensor, not the roof interceptor.

items.sees: Delivery / utility eVTOL. A possible later carrier for a sensor, not an interceptor.
items.misses: C-UAS
items.risk: German airframe, civilian mission. Catalogue it as a mother-drone candidate.

items.sees: Nothing. This is the thing you fly at your own scanner.
items.misses: Do not use DJI as the interceptor. Closed stack, Chinese C2, no net, no open protocol.
items.risk: Best known inbound for a German garden test because the sky is full of them. C1/C2 class usually broadcasts RID. Mini / C0 under 250 g often does not.

items.name_en: DJI Mini class (C0, often no RID)
items.name_de: DJI Mini-Klasse (C0, oft ohne Remote ID)
items.sees: A quiet inbound. Many C0 Mini aircraft in Open category have no Direct Remote ID duty.
items.misses: Your RID-only scanner will look at a Mini and see sky.
items.risk: Use it to prove the acoustic layer. Do not use it to prove Remote ID.

items.sees: A 5 or 7 inch interceptor airframe you can print or buy as carbon
items.misses: Trust. This is the default FPV brain of the hobby. It is also the default brain of the other side.
items.risk: Fastest DIY intercept start, worst supply-chain story. Pixhawk / Auterion is the graduation.

items.design: PX4/Dronecode, Auterion (CH) in the commercial line
items.sees: An open autopilot you can task. MAVLink. The language a node can speak.
items.misses: A net. You still need a frame, motors, a catcher.
items.risk: Open stack. Auterion is Swiss and already sits in German Vector aircraft. Prefer this over nameless F405 boards for anything that leaves the garden.

items.make: home printer or EU carbon shops
items.sees: The airframe of a first interceptor. PETG or CF-PETG on a hardened printer, or a bought carbon plate.
items.misses: Motors, ESCs, props, battery, net, brains.
items.risk: Printing the frame at home is the one part that is actually local. Keep the STL in the repo.

items.design: open / police net guns / FPV net pods
items.make: DIY or DE/EU police suppliers later
items.sees: The only catcher this project will discuss for the roof layer
items.misses: A Shahed at 150 m/s. That is a later net, a later swarm, a later altitude.
items.risk: Legal: a net over your own inbound test drone on your own ground is a test. A net over a stranger's aircraft is not a weekend hobby.

items.sees: A European software layer over PX4 that governments already buy
items.misses: A cheap garden quad
items.risk: Swiss, not German, and already in the German stack. Talk to them when intercept leaves the printer.

items.sees: A European test inbound, if you refuse to put a DJI over the house
items.misses: The statistical sky. Most of what actually flies here is still DJI.
items.risk: Better origin. Worse as a representative attacker.
